title: QwQ-32B Operating Regime Analysis

aggregate_c0.note: effective = problems with multi-candidate AND successful constraint extraction

experiments.per_problem_vote_distribution: all 22 problems have exactly 1 candidate answer
experiments.conclusion: SICA structurally identical to SC; zero answer divergence across all 22 problems

multi_candidate_details.note: SICA scored minority True=38 > majority False=27, flipping correct SC answer

experiments.root_cause: QwQ-32B re-reasons during extraction prompt instead of outputting structured JSON; 3/4 multi-candidate problems got 0 constraints
experiments.conclusion: SICA 5.9pp worse than SC; constraint extraction failure + scoring bias

experiments.note: Only 2-problem live test completed before model pivot; N too small for analysis
experiments.conclusion: SICA identical to SC; insufficient data
Zero answer divergence even at T=1.0; reasoning model's deterministic chain dominates sampling randomness

key_findings: QwQ-32B produces near-zero answer divergence on math domain (AIME: 0/22 problems with >1 candidate, MATH: 0/5 across 3 temperatures)
Logic domain shows some nominal diversity (23.5%) but constraint extraction fails on 75% of multi-candidate problems
The ONE problem where SICA had constraints + multi-candidate (498_Q8), it picked the WRONG answer (minority with higher constraint score)
Net effect: SICA identical to SC on math, 5.9pp WORSE than SC on logic
Root cause: reasoning model's extended chain-of-thought produces deterministic conclusions regardless of sampling temperature
Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct achieves C0=46% on same problem types, validating that SICA requires non-reasoning models for trace diversity

operating_regime_boundary.verdict: QwQ-32B operates outside SICA's effective regime (C0=2.6% << 20% threshold). Reasoning models eliminate trace diversity, making constraint-based aggregation structurally vacuous.
operating_regime_boundary.implication_for_paper: Validates Claim 2: SICA has a well-defined operating regime bounded by model capability. Too-strong models (reasoning) collapse diversity; SICA degenerates to SC or worse.

conclusion: Reasoning models eliminate trace diversity, making constraint-based aggregation structurally vacuous. SICA requires sufficient answer disagreement (C0 >= 20%) to provide value over simple majority voting.
